# SK2010 — A string comparison has an implicit culture policy

<!-- Generated from Rules/Rikarin.Skala.Rules.Metadata/rules.json. Do not edit. -->

A string.Compare overload omits a culture/comparison argument, or parameterless ToLower/ToUpper is used directly in equality.

| | |
|---|---|
| Category | Correctness |
| Default severity | warning |
| Scope | Semantic |
| Needs a compilation | yes |
| Fix | no |
| Language version floor | — |
| Since | 2.0 |

## Why

Ambient culture can change comparison outcomes across machines or requests. The correct policy may be linguistic or ordinal; spelling that policy explicitly keeps it independent of an accidental process setting.

## Example

Instead of:

```csharp
return string.Compare(left, right) == 0;
```

Write:

```csharp
return string.Equals(left, right, StringComparison.Ordinal);
```

## When it does not fire

Only bound System.String methods are inspected. Explicit CultureInfo or StringComparison overloads, invariant casing and display-oriented casing outside a direct == or != expression are ignored. The rule also accepts an explicit ignoreCase argument only when a culture is specified; a bool alone still uses ambient culture. Custom lookalikes are excluded. No fix chooses between ordinal, invariant or user-culture semantics.

## Configuration

- `dotnet_diagnostic.SK2010.severity`
